notes.title: The Monument Update Has Arrived
notes.content:
Hi everyone, István here!

Its been a long time coming but version 1.2 is finally here and there's a lot to cover so lets get right to it!

[h1]Monuments[/h1]
Version 1.2 is dubbed the "Monument Update" because I've added 5 monuments to the kingdom of Anceps. Without spoiling too much These monuments grant the player passive buffs, such as health regen or longer shields.

A monument can be found on each of the main levels of the game. By default the monument menu can be accessed with TAB or clicking the Right Stick on the controller.

[h1]Stat reworks[/h1]
How the player's stats (HP, Mana and Stamina) are modified throughout a gameplay session have been changed.
Previously by defeating bosses the player would gain stats and when igniting bonfires would lose mana (this mana was regainable after defeating the area boss).

This system is now completely replaced with a leveling system based on enemy kills. This system allows for a more gradual gain of stats and the possibility to farm levels if someone is stuck on a boss. Every 5th level the damage of the spells gain a small buff as well.

[h1]Other notable changes[/h1]
Thanks to GameMaker Studio 2.3.2 release, an issue with high refresh rate monitors have been solved. Previously this issue meant that anyone running a high refresh rate monitor would only be able to play the game at 45ish FPS instead of the required 60.

9slice now have been applied to every UI box on the screen. This improve the clarity of the UI elements and the overall feel of the game.

Following up with this, the ability to resize the game window while in windows mode have been added. It supports resolutions 720p, 768p, 900p, 1080p and 1440p, but the window can also be manually resized without introducing black bars if the scale is not 16:9.

[h2]Small fixes/changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Slight performance improvements were gained due to GameMaker Studio 2 update.
[*] The camera does not zoom in anymore while talking to NPCs.
[*] Fixes missing gate opening sounds.
[*] Improved the textures of the castle palace.
[*] Various small things I forgot about.
[/list]



I would like to thank every one of you who supports the development of the game for sticking with me for so long. Version 1.2 is the most complete version of Blue Flame to date and I hope you have as much fun playing it as much fun I had making it.

[i]István[/i]

notes.title: Patch #2 (v1.1.0.3) is out!
notes.content:
Hello everyone, István here!

It's time for another regular update of Blue Flame and this time it's a reworked first level. 

[h2]Reworked Last Battlefield[/h2]

The Last Battlefield was the first level ever created to the game and so it needed an update greatly.

The new version retains the level's original premise, but makes it harder to get lost, while still having an open battlefield to explore.

Due to changes in the structure and accessible places in the first level, old saves will not load the new Last Battlefield. To reach the new Last Battlefield you have to start a new game.

[h2]Fixes and Updates[/h2]

The following fixes and updates have also appeared:
[list]
[*] Autosave have been disabled as it could cause issues with being spawn-killed (Spawn killing is bad, m'kay?)
[*] Archers have received updates to their depths and directions, and they won't face east now every time.
[*] Texture prefetching in loading has been segmented to aid with freezing while loading.
[*] Surface sizes have been changed to be a power of 2 to improve performance.
[*] Blinding Light spell has been slightly reworked.
[/list]

[h2]Upcoming Updates[/h2]

In our last patch I promised a Hungarian translation of the game as well. That translation is still coming, but because the reworked Battlefield is a complete package I decided to release it separately.

In the following weeks expect translation to Hungarian, then to other languages as well and updated shadows to the objects of the game. Later down the line a few NPCs might appear in the game.

Until then, don't forget to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/FSSBlueFlame]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/FSSBlueFlame]Facebook[/url] and join our [url=https://discord.gg/Gm6vzEd]Discord[/url] server.

[i]István[/i]

notes.title: Blue Flame 1.0 Is Here!
notes.content:
Hi everyone, István here!

It's been a long journey, but we finally reached the end. Or the beginning?

The time has come for Blue Flame to be released and I'm super happy to share it with everyone. Blue Flame has been a passion project of mine for years and it's finally here for everyone.

I would like to thank everyone who's been part of the development process, be it anyone from the development team or from the community for their amazing work so that Blue Flame can be release.

[h3]What's in the release?[/h3]

Blue Flame 1.0 contains seven levels each with their own bosses. The base game should be around 3-4 hours long from start to finish.

[h3]What do you mean base game?[/h3]

As explained in the roadmap post, Blue Flame will be updated through the year. First up is an update that will bring a lot of quality of life changes as well as balance changes. After that we're planning content updates that are yet to be revealed.


[h3]Where can I reach out to the devs?[/h3]

The easiest is to join our [url=https://discord.gg/Gm6vzEd]Discord server[/url] but we're very active on [url=https://twitter.com/fssblueflame]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://facebook.com/fssblueflame]Facebook[/url] as well. We're also checking our [url=mailto:info@fssblueflame.com]emails[/url] daily.


Thank you for trying out the game and I hope you'll have a great time!

[i]István[/i]

notes.title: Roadmap for 2021
notes.content:
Hi everyone István here, your friendly Blue Flame developer.

In my last post I started a devlog series, that quickly turned into nothing, because as it turns out raising a puppy [url=https://twitter.com/FSSBlueFlame/status/1335307773681278982/photo/1](look at her, omg so cute)[/url] working 8 hours a day, developing a game, maintaining a social life and a devlog is kinda hard, I talked about what's still left to do in the game. 

Well, some of that is still left to do, but today I'm here to talk about what can you except from the game post launch. Here's the roadmap:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37519229/ca91e43d089f6bb9032df3f17363771ba7ae7482.png[/img]

Let's break this image down. Let's start with the obvious, the game launches on the 29th of January.

[h2]Update 1.1[/h2]

Update 1.1 is gonna be a patch that will contain a lot of player feedback. Since this is a solo project and while I have a clear vision of the game, I got limited feedback regarding some aspects of the game. This patch's aim will be to get more feedback an incorporate that into the game as well as some boss encounter updates. I'm estimating to release this 1-1.5 month after the game's initial release.

[h1]EXTRA! EXTRA! EXTRA![/h1]

[h2]Update 1.2[/h2]

This is gonna be a bigger one. Update 1.2 brings new free content to everyone who owns the game. New interesting underground levels that tie into the game's world and expands it's lore. One of the key NPC's of this update will be Loremaster Sebastian. I'm planning to get this content update to everyone at the beginning of the summer.

[h2]Update 1.3 & 1.4[/h2]

Both of these updates will add extra content to the game with update 1.3 featuring the hills of the Dragonpeak mountain and update 1.4 featuring the still functioning, but isolated community of the last pyromancers. I'm planning to release theses update at the end of the summer and at the 2021 holiday season.

Of course between these larger updates I'll be making sure to bugfix as much as possible with what little time I have.

I hope you all as excited as I am for the game's release and future!

István

notes.title: Devlog #1 - The Road Ahead
notes.content:
Hey Everyone, Steve here!

It has been a while since I wrote any kind of Devlogs, so a quick recap: I'm a solo developer from Hungary, working after work hours on my first commercial project, Blue Flame, a top-down action game in which you play as a pyromancer in a world where flames only emitt cold. I've been at this project for on and off - mostly off - for around 5 years now, but over the last 1.5 years I started to take the whole project seriously.

Fast forward 1.5 years, small amounts of work every day and the game is nearly done. It's both exciting and frightening at the same time. There's still some stuff left to do, so let's see how my faithful Hack'n'Plan milestone is doing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37519229/f75641bd433452a9a5bb123ff808f5987239029b.png[/img]

The reason I like to look at this board is because it actually calms me down. It's nice to see that it's only basically a work week worth of work (try to say this many times fast), but this doesn't cover the whole story. Because this milestone is continuously growing at an alarming rate. Sometimes very basic things pop into my head, like achievements, and I'll have to assign time to it. One could argue that this is just feature creep, but not really. This is just stuff that I haven't written down because I'm a dumdum.

I'll have the next week of from work, so I can try to do as much as I can - suck it, Cyberpunk 2077 - and hopefully by the end of the week I'll have most of the content done. "But what's actually missing from the game?" I hear you ask, because so far I haven't done anything but just wasted your time, so here's the most important stuff that's missing and most likely I will work on it in the following order:

[list]
[*] The Enchantress
[*] King Gawain
[*] Sikla Castle
[*] The Gatekeeper
[*] Extra enemies
[*] The Archmage
[/list]

In theory this list doesn't look that bad, but if there's something I've learned over the last few years is that theory is one thing. To end this post on a positive note, a community member suggested adding barrels that can explode into the game. Here's how that turned out:

[url=https://twitter.com/FSSBlueFlame/status/1337410008800256002]https://twitter.com/FSSBlueFlame/status/1337410008800256002[/url]


Join me in next week's devlog to see, what I've managed to reach in my one week of game development. If you'd like to be more involved in the game's development, you can join our [url=https://discord.gg/Gm6vzEd]Discord[/url] as well.

[u]Steve[/u]

notes.title: Version 0.5 is out!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I'm excited to bring you the newest update of Blue Flame, version 0.5! Let's jump right into it with the main course.

[h2]The Forgotten Docks[/h2]

V0.5 opens up a new area called the Forgotten Docks. While currently not implemented this area will unlock the fast travel mechanic of the game that will enable you to travel to the Crossroad Tavern or to the Road to Sikla Castle.

This level also feature a new spell, the Firemine that's perfect for players who would like to lure enemies into traps.
[h2]
Champion of the Battlefield[/h2]

A new boss has arrived to the game! This boss replaces the Daeodon at the beginning of the game and serves as a tutorial boss that teaches the players the importance of blocking and dashing.

[h2]Additions and updates[/h2]

The following have been added/updated in the game:
[list]
[*] Options menu have been added. It's not fully completed yet, but a lot of options (such as particles, screenshake and volumes) can be tweaked.
[*] Added missing animations for Skeleton Halberd and balances.
[*] Crystals now slowly pulse with their lighting.
[*] Spawner bush now has the possibility to delay the spawning of the Crawler enemy.
[*] Taking screenshots with F12 now use a sequential numbering.
[*] Improved the performance of animation rendering.
[*] Updated dialogs to match the lore of the game.
[*] Updated controller view so it reverts back to the player if the Right Stick is not in use.
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]

The following have been fixed in the game:

[list]
[*] Firesword can no longer hit dead enemies.
[*] Menu can be used with a controller.
[*] About menu buttons now snap correctly.
[*] Fixed an issues that made the potions unable to be picked up if it spawned near a dead Shielder.
[/list]


In the upcoming weeks a new version of the game will come out that will feature a new level of the game as well as the aforementioned fast-travel mechanic.

[i]Steve[/i]

notes.title: Patch 0.4.9.1 Is Out!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Version 4.9.1 is out and while it's only a small increment from version 0.4.9.1 it feels like it should be a whole new, much bigger patch.

Let's get right into it and start with the biggest change, the controller.

[h2]Controller input[/h2]

We are now confident enough in the controller input to remove it from experimental status. While the prompts still show the keyboard input you can now seamlessly switch between using the controller or mouse and keyboard. Further refinements for the controller input (such as rumbling) will arrive in following patches.

The controller layout:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37519229/259c793d82fbc2216df0d077b82e0db5a6ccb73a.png[/img]

[h2]Updates and Polishes[/h2]

In the latest patch the following things have been updated and/or polished:

[list]
[*][b] UPDATED MAIN MENU[/b] - The menu now contains the new key art and switching to full screen snaps the buttons to the lower left corner
[*] [b]EXPLODING SKELETON[/b] - A new enemy appeared in the Cemetery of the Ignoble, a skeleton that rises from the ground and charges the player.
[*] The Options, saves and screenshots folder is now located un User/AppData/Local/Blue_Flame as opposed to User/AppData/Local/BlueFlame_GMS2
[*] Input controller has been reworked so that the player now can switch seamlessly between mouse and keyboard or controller.
[*] Controller camera movement has been adjusted in a way that it reverts back to the player if the right stick is not used.
[*] A quick boss tease against the Maggot of the Underworld has been added to the Last Battlefield
[*] Crystal lights are now more dynamic, changing in size and color.
[*] Halberd Skeleton now has proper attack and death animations, with correct attack range and angle.
[*] Added grass to Aaron's garden in the Crossroad Tavern.
[*] When changing rooms the selected spell now stays the same. Before it reverted back to Combustion.
[*] Bushes now can be traversed if burnt.
[*] Controller setting screen has been removed as it is now obsolete.
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]

The following fixes have been added:

[list]
[*] Daeodon has been banished from the Last Battlefield [strike]to the Shadow Realm[/strike] for causing a crash to desktop.
[*] Fixed hitboxes of the graves.
[*] Reworked save/load system to circumvent an issues with spells resetting after entering the Cemetery of the Ignoble
[/list]

There is currently a known issue with the "About the Demo" screen's buttons not snapping correctly to the bottom left. I'm working on it.


[h2]What's next?[/h2]

Hopefully in the following weeks I'll be able to get a new sub-level to the game that acts as a quick-travel point as well as the long awaited options menu. High on the priority list is also the rework of the intro.

I hope You'll have fun in the latest update of Blue Flame

[i]Steve[/i]

notes.title: The Cemetery Of the Ignoble
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I'm pleased to let you all know, version 0.4.9.0 is now out. This area contains a brand new level called the Cemetery of the Ignoble.

[h1]The Cemetery of the Ignoble[/h1]

East of the Forsaken Village lies The Cemetery of the Ignoble engulfed in fog and in it's center the Crypt of the Royal blood with it's fearsome protector.

The Cemetery is a place full of undead skeletons ready to attack anyone who enters. The graves of this cemetery are long abandoned and contains souls that drain you sanity. Do you have what it takes to conquer this area?

[h2]Fixes, improvements and new things[/h2]

In this new version the following things have been updated, improved and added:

[*] [b]Mass Grave and Cemetery of the Ignoble areas[/b]
[*] [b]New Logo![/b]
[*] Full screen in-game now does not letterbox, but extends the view
[*] Skeleton Swordman and Skeleton archer have been added
[*] If dashing with less than 50% stamina the player now grunts
[*] Various improvements to camera handling
[*] Added new level selector cheat: Pressing 0 brings up the cheat menu, entering [i]room_goto[/i] brings up an input field, enter the following to go to these levels:
[list]
 [*] rm_battlefield - Last Battlefield
 [*] rm_hub - Crossroad Tavern
 [*] rm_battlefield_tavern - West Road
 [*] rm_hub_forest - North Road
 [*] rm_shifting_woods - Shifting Woods
 [*] rm_narrow_pass - Narrow Pass
 [*] rm_forsaken_village - Forsaken Village
 [*] rm_village_cemetery - Mass Grave
 [*] rm_cemetery - Cemetery of the Ignoble
[/list]
[*] Unused levels. These levels were from an earlier build of the game, but can be interesting for those who would like to explore unused/cut content. Expect game crashes with some of these rooms.
[list]
 [*] rm_cemetery_old - Older version of the Cemetery
 [*] rm_shifting_woods_old - Older Shifting Woods
 [*] rm_catacomb_lavalake
 [*] rm_dilapdated

[/list]
[*] The Necrolith - Originally planned as a boss of the Cemetery the Necrolith is a three headed monster, that will serve as a great foe in the Crypt.
[*] A lot of small improvements and tweaks.
[/list]


[h2]Known Issues[/h2]

[list]
[*] With the new full screen system the menus are displaying incorrectly if full screens is used.
[*] The Halberd skeleton incorrectly uses the Skeleton Swordman's attack animation
[/list]


I hope you all like the new updated, adjacent to this new area another one will come, called the Docks in the next update.

[i]Steve[/i]

notes.title: The guys behind Blue Flame
notes.content:
Let's get the obvious out of the way: Blue Flame is a top down action game where you play as a pyromancer. It is heavily inspired by the Souls franchise (specifically 1 and 2).

[h3]The game[/h3]

The idea of the game came to mind a few years ago as a small game consisting of a few levels. It was actually going to be a platformer and was called Bond of a Pyromancer, but by nature a platformer is more disconnected from reality than a top down game, so the perspective was changed quickly. After a while the development stopped, but around a year ago the project was reignited. (See what I did there?)

The graphical direction of the game was changed, thanks to Tom, who created a system with which we can use Blender models to create the animation, akin to the one done in Dead Cells. This immensely cuts down costs on developing and creates smooth 24 FPS animations. It can be turned up to 60, we'll see about that ;)

Now the plan is a late 2020 release with around 7 levels - 3 of it is playable in the demo - interesting stories told through the NPCs, areas to explore and cool spells that can be unlocked. The current demo is more like a "proof of concept" or a larger vertical slice. A New demo will be released at the end of the year, before the release of the game, most likely will still only contain the current levels, but much more polished and if significant gameplay changes are made those included as well.

[h3]The team[/h3]

The creator and the programmer of the world is Steve Szilágyi, who does all the coding, world building and lore creation. His best friend Tom Gálffy helps him with infinite wisdom and memes regarding design choices.

The music and sound effects are outsourced to Alex Gobbet, the pixel art is made by Jurica Cvetko and the models are done by Rowan Cruse Howse with Steve creating the simple models and animating all of them.

[h3]The future[/h3]

Since Blue Flame has been in the back of my mind for years now and it all started as a small project, I fully inted to finish it this year, even tho it's unfortunately not my full time job right now. After the release of the game, there will be a few updates addig new content and extra area to explore.

I hope you'll like our demo, we did pour our soul into it, if you did, give us a holler on our Discord server.

Steve

notes.title: Patch 0.4.5.2 released
notes.content:
Hello everyone, Steve here!

This version of the game is the penultimate before the Steam Demo rolls out on the 9th of June, so let's see what's changed!

[h1]Shifting Woods[/h1]

Hands down the most important change is the rework of the Shifting Woods level, with the addition of moving trees. Explore the new level and try not to get lost in it. With this level rework Wassa received a buff as well and got regenerative properties. Loremaster Sebastian arrived in this reworked Forest as well, he might tell you a thing or two about how to defeat the improved Wassa.

[h1]Save/Load system[/h1]

A Save/Load system has been added to the game. As of right now hitting ESC while playing saves the game and returns to the title screen. Clicking on the Continue button returns you to the game - as expected - but starting a new game erases the current save file. There's only one save file right now, but in the future, there will be multiple. 

With this the persistent levels have been turned off, so you can start new playthroughs of the game without having to restart it. There might be some bugs in the save system, especially if you're dying in a room without an activated bonfire.

[h1]Changes[/h1]

Let's get into the smaller changes:

[list]
[*] New sounds have been added to the game, including hurt and death sound effects for Daeodon
[*] Killing Daeodon now triggers a camera toggle so we can always see him die.
[*] Footstep sounds have been decreased.
[*] Potion pickups have been reworked. Now there's a potion dropped on the ground when an enemy is killed (and it can give a potion) but that potion can only be picked up if there's no aggroed enemy nearby.
[*] Fixed various camera issues, talking with NPCs now has a smaller zoom in.
[*] Textboxes now don't disappear automatically, but a close popup appears once the NPC is done talking.
[*] Dot product have been disabled, this means that when fighting enemies you no longer walk when going backward.
[*] HP bar now flashes white when you're hit (the final polish of this is currently a work in progress)
[*] Two new small levels have been added that currently serve as end-of-demo levels. Later they will lead to new areas in the game.
[*] Fixed various bugs and instabilities.
[/list]


[h1]Known issues[/h1]

[list]
[*] Moving trees can get into the way of the player.
[*] Attack dogs can jump through fences and run away. #cowards
[*] Footsteps for the attack dogs are not perfect yet.
[/list]


There's less than a week until the demo of Blue Flame is out, that will feature three levels, I hope you're as excited as I am.

[i]Steve[/i]

[h3]New Stuff:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added the ambiancer, ambiance sound effects now can be heard in the game world
[/list]

[h3]Known issues:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The game can only truly be restarted by restarting the whole app. This is due to the persistent level. (The Spooky Man)
[*] In the second intro scene there's overlapping of talking sound effects.
[*] Performance issues with the particles (Arkanio)
[/list]


I would like to thank our community members for uncovering these bugs If you too would like to participate, join our [url=https://discord.gg/UK5S4f6]Discord[/url] group and let us know you're interested.


Steve

notes.title: Development Log #2
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

As we're prepping for the Steam Game Festival with our demo, there's a lot of stuff that went into the game, I'd like to only highlight a few of them.

[h3]Demo build submitted[/h3]
Probably the single most important thing that happened in the last two weeks, is we set up the Demo page for Blue Flame and submitted a demo for approval. The deadline is May 15th, so we are in time, but we still have some minor things that will need to be fleshed out once the demo build goes like in June.

[h3]Intro[/h3]
I've added an intro text to the game, so far it's bare bones but it will be upgraded more in the final version of the game. It conveys the base setting of the game in a few sentences and sets you up for the adventure.

[h3]Loading art[/h3]
Previously what we had is just a basic loading screen, but now we have renders for the upcoming levels. These indicate slightly how the level will look like, and creates a better atmosphere for the game. The loading screen of the Forsaken Village is this week's cover image.

[h3]UI autoscale[/h3]
One thing that was issue for a while is the inability to automatically scale up the UI of the game when switching to Full Screen mode. Well, NO MORE! We now have a UI that scales up if you enter full screen mode.

[h3]The Ambiancer[/h3]
While this is a work in progress still, Alex created some great ambiance sounds for the game, that currently includes rain, wind gusting and leaves rustling effects. These will be played very faintly to the player so that they give just that right amount of feel to the game.

[h3]Control(er) updates[/h3]
This will not be obvious to the player but a controller class is slowly getting implemented into the game. What is means is basically rebindable keys along with a lot more stability. The controller support has also been updated, and now the left and right sticks move the camera together. This results in a faster more snappy-er system that similar to how the game handles with keyboard and mouse.

[h3]A lot more[/h3]
Remember, these have just been highlights, a lot of small fixes and improvements went into the whole cycle. Don't forget to follow us on social media if you'd like to see more about the development of the game.

Steve

notes.title: Development Log #1
notes.content:
Hello everyone Steve here!

I'd like to share a quick blog post about what we've been working on in the Development Cycle of Blue Flame.

[h1]Porting to GameMaker Studio 2[/h1]

Up until this point Blue Flame was developed in GameMaker: Studio 1.4.9999 due to the actual development starting around 5 years ago, but getting abandoned. Originally the game was supposed to be developed in GMS 1.4 and after the game is done I'd switch to GMS2, but I decided to give the importer another go and imported to current project into GMS2. It had - perhaps still has - some hiccups, but for the most part we can say it was smooth sailing and the game in now in GMS2. Working on already created levels will be a trouble in the future due to how GMS2's level editor differs from GMS1.4's, but luckily these levels are mostly done.

With the port to GMS2 we also had a big improvement in performance so there shouldn't be an issue with micro-stuttering. This port will also allow us to export the game to Ubuntu and macOS as well, in a future post we'll talk more about that as well.

[h1]Giving sound to the world[/h1]

We're getting ready to the Steam Game Festival, this meant that we have now two amazing boss music and a ton of new audio effect to breath life into the game. From the minor stuff of ambiance wind gusts to a whole pack of effects for an enemy, we have it all.

[h1]New art, new NPC encounter[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37519229/7027106643a27464300fb27dabff8c2ae2dfe088.gif[/img]

Thanks to our very talented artist we now have a key building in the game, I'd rather not tell too much information about it now, but it's a key location in the game and will be available in the full version of the game.

Jotal can also be encountered in the Crossroad Tavern whereas before he only showed up in the Forsaken Village.



That's all for today, folks don't forget to wishlist the game and follow us on social media for more!

[i]- Steve[/i]
